clue.text: Key Socialist speech displays refinement

parts.note: E is a musical key
LAB is the short form of Labour, Britain's socialist party
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A leading left-wing politician's address shows polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Working a plan out in finer detail is a way of polishing and improving it.

clue.text: Retiring chum is a real gem

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for chum is read backwards

parts.note: a pal is a chum
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for a friend who is a real treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like a description of a shy friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapis lazuli is a deep blue semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Ban imposed by former Yorkshire captain

explanation.surface: A prohibition put in place by an ex-skipper of a cricket county.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott captained Yorkshire, an English county cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: A boycott is a collective refusal to deal with someone, and it is also the surname of a famous cricketer.

clue.text: Overcharges for first film prints

explanation.surface: A cinema bills too much for early copies of a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush customers is slang for charging them too much; rushes are the first unedited prints from a day's filming.

clue.text: Made Tina curt — very curt

indicators.note: made in the sense of fashioned, so these letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Tina was made very short with people.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserved and saying little is close to being brusque or abrupt.

clue.text: Excel in public work

parts.note: overt means open or public
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Advice to shine in work done for the community.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise above or surpass others is to outdo them.

clue.text: One simpatico to the friendly spectre of Communism

parts.note: kind means friendly
red is the colour of Communism
a spectre is a ghost or spirit

explanation.surface: An allusion to the spectre haunting Europe in the Communist Manifesto, made friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A like-minded person who shares your outlook is someone sympathetic to you.

clue.text: Try one way to become a writer

parts.note: an essay is an attempt or try
the Roman numeral I is one
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: One attempt at taking up authorship.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes short prose pieces is an author.

clue.text: Disenchanted after having solved anagrams

explanation.surface: Someone has lost the magic after cracking word puzzles.
explanation.walkthrough: Solving an anagram breaks a spelling apart into a new word, a play on breaking an enchantment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ending a magic charm frees the one enchanted; cracking a jumble of letters is the punning second sense.

clue.text: Suggest using wood one metre thick

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
ply is a thin layer of wood, as in plywood

explanation.surface: Advice to use a plank a metre thick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one metre thick' describes the wood in the surface; 'using' and 'thick' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something without stating it outright is to suggest it.

clue.text: One of life's winners or one who inherits

parts.note: someone who does well in life is called a success
taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between a high achiever and an heir.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface looks like two definitions joined by 'or', but 'or' gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever follows on and takes over a title or estate is the next heir in line.

clue.text: Doesn't his conversion seem insincere?

indicators.note: a conversion changes a thing into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a man's religious conversion is a sham.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the nine letters of DOESNTHIS; 'seem' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untruthful or deceitful is not sincere.

clue.text: Follow by rail

explanation.surface: Advice to travel after someone by train.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to follow them; a railway line is also called a track.

clue.text: For actors it represents fair play

explanation.surface: A theatre body stands for justice.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the trade union for British actors; the word also means fairness and even-handed justice.

clue.text: US government employs pawnbrokers in the morning

parts.note: uncle is old British slang for a pawnbroker
AM means before noon

explanation.surface: Washington hires pawnshop owners for the morning shift.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in a top hat personifies the American state.

clue.text: Monk serves gin to priest first

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for game
first is written 1ST, and the figure 1 looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: A monk pours a gin and gives it to a priest before anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' seems to say the gin comes first; it is 1ST read as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cistercian of the strict La Trappe observance is a member of a monastic order.

clue.text: He can barely help but disrupt the match!

definitions.text: He can barely help but disrupt the match!

parts.words: He can barely help but disrupt the match!
parts.note: barely means naked: someone who runs onto a sports pitch with no clothes on interrupts play

explanation.surface: A fan who just cannot stop himself ruining the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A naked pitch invader halts a sporting fixture.

clue.text: Bond offered protection against espionage

explanation.surface: A secret agent called Bond guards against spies.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a financial security; measures against spies are security too.

clue.text: A girl he mistreated in N. Carolina

indicators.note: something mistreated is handled badly, so these letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A woman was abused by a man in a Southern state.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Sir Walter, this city is the state capital of North Carolina.

clue.text: Struggle to deliver bundle containing two tons

indicators.note: containing means the word for bundle holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a bale is a large bound bundle, as of hay
T is the abbreviation for ton, so two tons are two Ts

explanation.surface: Someone toils to deliver a heavy package of two tons.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight or hard contest is a struggle.

clue.text: Zionist leader about to break into song in America

indicators.note: to break into means these letters force their way inside the word for song

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word

parts.note: on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A Zionist chief is about to burst into song in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as one phrase meaning 'on the point of', but the words split: 'about' supplies letters and 'to break into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A southwestern state is a part of the USA.

clue.text: Austere cleric comes back into view

indicators.note: into means the turned letters go inside the word for view

parts.note: to see is to view

indicators.note: comes back means the short word for cleric is read in reverse

parts.note: REV is short for Reverend, a cleric

explanation.surface: A stern clergyman reappears in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' reads as the cleric returning, but it signals the turnaround; 'into' is the container signal, and 'view' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and austere are synonyms for strict and stern.

clue.text: One trade for a model

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to deal is to trade or do business

explanation.surface: A single business exchange made to serve as a pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example to follow is a paragon or model.

clue.text: Restoring balance by having an afternoon in bed?

explanation.surface: Someone recovers equilibrium by lazing about all afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: someone who lies in all afternoon is still up only by evening, as if 'evening up' meant rising then.
explanation.definitionFit: Making things equal again is levelling; the joke reads it as getting out of bed at nightfall.

clue.text: Toil to use a coffee-mill

explanation.surface: Hard work to operate a coffee grinder.
explanation.definitionFit: Grind means tedious hard labour, and also to crush beans to powder.

clue.text: Having trouble finding how to preserve vegetables

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to work out how to keep their garden produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a fix or a mess is an idiom for trouble; vegetables kept in vinegar are literally steeped in brine.

clue.text: Window in an Oxford college

explanation.surface: A window in one of the Oxford colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay window projecting from an upper floor is one sense; another names a college of Oxford University.

clue.text: Supervisors prosecute workmen

parts.note: to charge someone is to accuse them formally in court
hands are manual workers, as in farmhands

explanation.surface: Foremen take legal action against their labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: Foremen in charge of a gang of workers are their supervisors.
